To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
ethanol-induced lipid interdigititation increases the proton permeability of phospholipid membranes.
proton permeability in DPPC membranes increases dramatically at the concentration of ethanol that is required to induce the formation of a fully interdigitated lipid gel state.
the proton permeability in DPPC large vesicles is markedly increased by the formation of the alcohol-induced fully interdigitated state of the phospholipid.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of alcohol on the structure and dynamics of phospholipid membranes.
the effect of alcohol on the structure of lipid bilayer membranes and on the proton permeability of lipid membranes.
the effects of lipid interdigitation, induced by alcohols, on proton permeability of DPPC vesicle membranes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
alcohol-induced lipid interdigititation can cause an increase in proton permeation through lipid bilayers.
the alcohol-induced interdigitation of DPPC lipids leads to an increase in proton permeation across the membrane.
ethanol-induced lipid interdigititation in biological membranes can increase membrane permeability to small ions, such as protons.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the alcohol-induced lipid interdigitated gel phase is a very permeable phase, and that the alcohol-induced membrane interdigitation is an important factor for the alcohol-induced membrane perturbation and membrane permeability.

the ethanol-induced lipid phase transition is an important factor that contributes to the increased gastric mucosal permeability and that this effect is more important in the stomach than in the small intestine.
ethanol-induced lipid interdigititation is a key factor in ethanol's effects on membrane structure and function.

the ethanol-induced interdigitation of DPPC lipids causes an abrupt increase in the proton permeability, and this increase is likely to be due to the changes in membrane surface charge density and thickness.
